exposure: Theory of Planned Behavior constructs (Attitudes towards vaginal birth, Subjective norms, Perceived behavior control over vaginal birth)
outcome: Adolescents' intention towards childbirth options (preference for caesarean section)
cohort: The study participants were 480 high school students in Greece.
finding: Participants with a negative impression of vaginal birth had a 2.20-fold higher probability of reporting a preference for caesarean section, while higher scores on TPB constructs related to vaginal birth were associated with a lower probability of preferring caesarean section.
